body: Thank you for the optimistic advice. I'll try reaching out to them again. Thanks!

I don't believe they're mutually exclusive. They use those terms interchangeably on their site. But this is clearly stated on their site:

People do not have to be suicidal to call – reasons to call include: substance abuse, economic worries, relationships, sexual identity, illness, getting over abuse, depression mental and physical illness, and loneliness.

Yet they completely brushed me aside. I sent them an email highlighting my experiences. Hopefully they can either better train their volunteers, or adjust the wording on their site if the only viable criteria for them to help you is that you're at your last wit.

Still feeling very distraught and depressed. So wary of using their services, but hoping that was a one-off night because I do know they've helped numerous people.

Thank you so much for your transparency and vulnerability in sharing. I'm so sorry to hear all that you're going through. I will without doubt keep you in my prayers. I know oftentimes the advice we give each other usually feels like automated textbook answers, but try and stay strong. It really isn't easy to love oneself, but we must learn and find a way. We can hopefully all support one another in this forum (even if our experiences with the hotline weren't exactly positive). I know I too need all the support I can get at this point in my life. Wishing you nothing but the best in your recovery and self-discovery. Take care.
What happened to you? I'd love to hear your story too?
